test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 17 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: By way of the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, ____________ has been included in the list of Fundamental Rights as part of the Right to Freedom.

options.text: right to assemble peaceably and without arms
to practise any profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business
protection against arrest and detention in certain cases

solution:
The correct answer is __**right to education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right to Education **

 
 
• The **Eighty-sixth Amendment** to the Indian Constitution guarantees the **right to early childhood care** until the age of six and the **right to education** for children aged six to fourteen.
 
• It has replaced **Article 45 (Early Childhood Education)** of the Directive principles of State policy and has inserted **Article 21A (Right to Education as a Fundamental Right) below Article 21.**
 
• It amended **Article 51A (Fundamental Duties) **to add a new duty of parents to provide education to their child between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
• Article 21A states that ***“The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine."***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• However, this right was finally implemented in **2010** after eight years.
 
• **India** joined a select group of nations on** April 2, 2010**, when a historic law declaring every child's right to education went into effect.
 
• The implementation of this was announced by former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.
 
• Article 45 was replaced as ***“The State shall endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.”***
 
• Article 51A states that **“who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.”**
